thread:
Jessica L.: Quick heads-up — running a throughput sweep for the Nebula Health POC tomorrow 09:00 PT. Primary goals: validate sustained qps, measure p95/p99 across ramp profiles, and confirm KMS/HSM integration doesn't blow tail latency. Also need final pricing ask for burst vs reserved.
Matt P.: Got it. Can you drop the load plan + expected payload sizes?
Jessica L.: Payloads are mixed: 70% short prompts (~50 tokens), 20% medium (~200 tokens), 10% long (~800 tokens). We'll test model: open-llama-70b-quant and a quantized 4-bit variant. Ramp plan: 10m linear ramp to target, sustain 30m, ramp down 5m. Targets: 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 qps.
Raj S.: For the HSM/KMS question — are they using Cloud KMS over TLS, or an on-prem HSM with separate network hop? That changes latency a lot.
Jessica L.: Customer will use customer-managed Cloud KMS via VPC peering to our private deployment. They asked about on-prem HSM later but not for this POC. So expect an extra 5–10ms per encryption op if KMS calls are in-path. Need to quantify effect on p99.
Sophie M.: Ops note — please enable KV cache prefixing for the short prompts to get realistic savings. Also record KV cache hit rate.
Jessica L.: Agree. We'll enable prefix cache and run two variants: cache-on and cache-off. Add these to the plan.
Matt P.: Can ops-bot schedule the run and post the exact cli we use? Also need spike test: a 60s microburst to 3x sustained qps to validate queue/backpressure.
ops-bot: Scheduling load run: start=2026-11-04T09:00:00-08:00, ramp=10m, sustain=30m, microburst at 15m for 60s, generator=vegeta-llm v0.9, targets=[500,1000,1500,2000], repeat each profile once.
Jessica L.: CLI for the runner (example):
```
veg load --target=https://redwood-poc.example/run \
  --ramp=10m --duration=30m --burst=60s --qps=1500 \
  --payload-template=payloads/mixed.json --concurrency=2000
```
Matt P.: For pricing — can we get an estimate for burst overage if they exceed reserved caps during the microburst? Also want per-token cost delta for quantized vs base model.
Raj S.: I'll crunch numbers after we get perf samples; preliminary note: quantized 4-bit reduces GPU throughput by ~1.8x but halves memory. So per-token cost may drop ~30–50% depending on batching. Provide a quick calc after first run.
Sophie M.: Security SQ follow-up — sec-qa-bot, can you confirm the KMS attestation / SOC2 items the customer asked about? They want an answer embedded in the results doc.
sec-qa-bot: Security checklist items required: SOC2 type II status (we are compliant), KMS integration guide (public doc link: https://redwood.example/docs/kms-integration), VPC peering runbook, key rotation policy summary. I will attach snippets to the post-run artifact.
Jessica L.: Great. A couple of enterprise blockers to flag so engineering can watch during the run: 1) VPC egress NAT mapping causing ephemeral port exhaustion at higher qps; 2) HSM/KMS call rate limits causing queueing; 3) cold-start penalty for model swaps when fallback triggers.
Matt P.: Noted. Ops, can you add netstat and ephemeral port metrics, and KMS latencies to the traces? Also capture kernel TCP_RETRANSMIT spikes.
ops-bot: Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, cpu/gpu util, net socket states, ephemeral ports, KMS call latency histogram (ms), KV cache hit rate, batch size distribution, ooms. Will push to the shared dashboard and export raw traces.
Raj S.: After the first 2 profiles, if p99 > 400ms we'll try: 1) increase batching, 2) enable small-ttl cache warming, 3) route to dedicated pool. We'll iterate.
Jessica L.: Can someone draft the short results template I'll send to the prospect? Need: 1) run summary + plots, 2) p50/p95/p99 table, 3) billing estimate for observed throughput (sustained + burst), 4) security answers attached. Keep it one page.
Sophie M.: I'll sketch it and share a draft here after run completes.
Matt P.: Last ask: include a short 'how we measured' section mentioning synthetic load generator, user-like payload mix, and KV cache toggles. Customer care about method.
Jessica L.: Perfect. Thanks team — we'll reconvene in thread once ops-bot posts raw numbers. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Run started (5342020001). Will post interim samples at each target finish.
Jessica L.: Thanks — tagging @Raj S. for the pricing calc when first samples are in.
